mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, Exalted is He, بَالغ أمره: الأمر is accusative by بالغ, because it has a future sense; it has also been read with annexation [بالغُ أمرِه]. Al-Farrāʾ permitted in ordinary speech بالغٌ أمرُه, with tanwīn, with الأمر nominative by بالغ, or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with بالغ its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of إنّ.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying واللائي يئسن: اللائي is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and يئسن with what follows it up to نسائكم is its ṣila (relative clause). وإن ارتبتم is a condition; فعدتهن is a mubtadaʾ, and ثلاثة أشهر its khabar (predicate); the فاء is the apodosis of the condition; and the condition with its apodosis and what is attached to it is a khabar about اللائي. The implied form is "if you are in doubt about them, then the term of their waiting period is three months". The singular of اللائي is التي.
His saying وَأولَات الْأَحْمَال: a mubtadaʾ; أجلهن is a second mubtadaʾ and أن يضعن the khabar — أن is in the position of the nominative, it and the verb being a maṣdar (verbal noun) — and the second [mubtadaʾ] with its khabar is the khabar of the first. It is also possible that أجلهن is a badal (substitute) of أولات, with أن يضعن the khabar, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). The singular of أولات is ذات.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying وَإِن كن أولات حمل: in كان is its noun and أولات is the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "if the divorced women are pregnant, then spend on them".

mekki-muskil:10-11.t:
His saying قد أنزل الله إِلَيْكُم ذكرا رَسُولا: ذكر is accusative by أنزل, and رسول is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ذكر, its implied form being "a reminder possessing a messenger" (ذكرا ذا رسول); then the muḍāf was omitted. It is also said that رسول is accusative as a badal (substitute) of ذكر, with رسول meaning a message (رسالة). It is also said that it is a badal and رسول is in its basic sense, but the meaning is "Allah has made manifest a reminder, a messenger", because أنزل indicates making manifest a matter that did not exist; so on this meaning it does not mean "a message". In both cases it is the badal of a thing for a thing that is identical to it.
It is also said that it is accusative by an implied أرسلنا ("We sent"); it is also said that it is accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"); it is also said that it is accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "follow a messenger" or "hold to a messenger"; it is also said that it is accusative by a verb that ذكرا indicates, its implied form being "Allah has sent down to you a reminder: remember a messenger" (تذكروا رسولا), or "so remember a messenger" (فذكر رسولا). It is also said that it is accusative by ذكر, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that governs as a verb does; its implied form is "Allah has sent down to you that you should remember a messenger".
His saying يتلو: a naʿt of رسول.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying لِتَعْلَمُوا: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تنزل; it is also said: to خلق.
